vision: A distributable library of AI coding assistant rules, skills, hooks, and an adversarial verification harness for Cursor and Claude Code. The library must dogfood its own authoring standards — including a rigorous, machine-validated state.json schema — before the library is considered trustworthy.
direction: library/cursor/ is the single source of truth for distributable config. Eval pipeline at 89.8% mean across 41 scenarios (12 at 100%, 35 above 80%, 3 below 70%). Full conversation trace capture operational. Active focus: close gaps (gap-14 session boundary 54%, gap-20 spike false positive 57%, routing_ambiguous 62%). New spikes: UI for .harness/ folder, eval accuracy improvements, prevent redundant re-planning, hooks tech debt audit. Priority 3 deferred: feat-13 multi-agent orchestration, feat-14 LLM-as-judge.

trade_offs.decision: Flat tasks array, not grouped buckets
trade_offs.reasoning: Hooks and agents iterate one list today; grouped buckets duplicate items and drift. harness-context.sh and harness_metrics.py can filter by status at read time.
Five hooks, harness_lint.py, HARNESS_STANDARD.md, and 27 eval scenarios already encode this lifecycle. done conflates verified and committed; doing conflates building and evaluating.

trade_offs.decision: Explicit type enum on every task
trade_offs.alternative: Infer type from id prefix only (feat-/gap-/spike-)
trade_offs.reasoning: Id prefixes are convention not validation; explicit type enables lint enforcement and clearer planner output.
22+ eval scenario seeds and 6 shell hooks read features today; alias prevents eval regression during phased rollout.
Preserves audit trail; metrics exclude cancelled from backlog counts.

trade_offs.alternative: Keep symlinks tracked, gitignore only transient files
trade_offs.reasoning: Matches how consumer projects treat IDE config; library/cursor/ is the distributable artifact
spec.md was read once (plan gate) then became stale. Single file eliminates drift by design.

tasks.name: Explore UI for .harness/ folder — visual dashboard for state, breadcrumbs, and contracts
tasks.details: Investigate building a lightweight UI (web or TUI) to visualize .harness/ contents: task board from state.json, breadcrumb timeline, contract status, eval scores over time. Could be a Cursor canvas, a local web app, or a CLI dashboard. Explore frameworks (React canvas, blessed/ink TUI, simple HTML report).

tasks.name: Improve eval accuracy — reduce UNCERTAIN verdicts and false positives
tasks.details: Current eval has 89.8% mean but still produces UNCERTAIN verdicts and false positives (e.g. spike-gate, ambiguous-escalate). Explore: (1) leverage conversation traces more aggressively in structural checks, (2) calibrate LLM judge prompts for subjective criteria, (3) add scenario-specific check overrides (e.g. skip negotiation_quality for spikes), (4) build a confusion matrix to identify systematic judge biases.

tasks.name: Prevent agent from re-creating plans that already exist
tasks.details: Agent sometimes launches /planner or rewrites state.json when a valid plan already exists with pending tasks. Explore: (1) add a pre-check in adversarial_harness.mdc — if state.json has pending tasks, skip planner and resume from next task, (2) harness-gate.sh could detect and warn, (3) add eval scenario to test 'resume vs re-plan' behavior. Related to routing_resume_existing (currently 100%) but covers edge cases where agent over-plans.

tasks.name: Audit hooks for technical debt and duplication
tasks.details: Hook scripts (contract-gate.sh, harness-context.sh, harness-gate.sh, evaluator-guard.sh) share repeated patterns: jq parsing of state.json, task iteration, status checks, path extraction. Explore: (1) extract shared functions into a hooks-lib.sh, (2) identify dead code paths, (3) check for inconsistent behavior between hooks (e.g. different fallback logic for features vs tasks), (4) verify all hooks handle edge cases (missing files, malformed JSON, empty arrays).
